actions.description: Call the acknowledged /mujoco/reset Trigger service; this is not a stop
actions.name: reset

outputs.description: Trigger response success flag from the reset callback
outputs.name: success

outputs.description: Trigger response message, including the callback error_sum text
outputs.name: message

facts.text: MjRos::init advertises /mujoco/reset with the reset_robot_service callback.

reset_robot_service takes a std_srvs/Trigger request, stops running effort controllers, resets the robot data, sleeps 100 model timesteps, sets response.success from an error_sum threshold and then restarts the controllers it stopped.
reset_robot creates new mjData, writes each robot joint qpos from joint_inits or zero, zeroes the joint qvel and qacc, zeroes the odometry velocities and calls mj_forward.
The simulate loop calls mj_step1 and mj_step2 continuously while ros::ok and adjusts the model timestep toward real time; it has no pause, stop or step-request branch.
main starts the simulate function on its own thread, next to three ROS setup threads.
publish_object_state_array returns without publishing when the configured rate is below 1E-9.
publish_joint_states returns without publishing when the configured rate is below 1E-9.
The shipped src/config/robot.yaml sets the object-state and joint-state publication rates to 0.0 for robot, world and spawned-object bodies.
MjRos::init advertises exactly the /mujoco/screenshot, /mujoco/reset, /mujoco/spawn_objects and /mujoco/destroy_objects services; no pause, stop or e-stop service is advertised.
The per-robot /<robot>/cmd_vel subscription is created only when at least one odometry joint is configured for that robot.
CmdVelCallback::callback writes the robot's six odometry velocity entries from the Twist, 0.0 for an axis without an odometry joint.

publish_object_state_array starts one thread each for robot, world and spawned-object bodies; each thread fills its own array and publishes it through the one object_state_array_pub publisher at its own rate.

determinism.notes: Event-driven recording fake with no physics step or pacing; the placeholder object and joint samples do not establish trajectory or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free RecordingRosTransport: it answers the declared reset service and the two subscriptions with placeholder messages and runs no MuJoCo engine, ros_control loop, ROS node or wall-clock pacing
the fake reset only increments a counter and returns a placeholder Trigger response; it does not reset mjData, restart controllers or reproduce the upstream error_sum check

the shipped src/config/robot.yaml sets all object-state and joint-state publisher rates to 0.0, so a live deployment must raise the relevant rate parameter before either observation can receive a fresh sample
the object and joint samples are placeholders and do not describe any loaded MJCF model; the real array sizes and body/joint names are scene-dependent

upstream publishes robot, world and spawned-object bodies as separate arrays on the same /mujoco/object_states topic at their own rates, so one live sample holds one body category; the fake always returns the same one-body placeholder array

the clone advertises no acknowledged pause, stop or e-stop; the effectful reset callback leaves the independent simulation thread stepping and restarts the effort controllers, so this package cannot claim a confirmed safe state
the package does not expose /mujoco/screenshot, /mujoco/spawn_objects, /mujoco/destroy_objects, the /<robot>/cmd_vel input, TF, marker arrays, base pose odometry or /mujoco/sensors_3D
